items.question: What's the cap on TODS panels at a single intersection approach?
items.note: Survey Procedures V.A (Pre-Interview): no more than six panels per intersection approach (G.S. 136-140.19(5)); if there is only room for one TODS assembly on the whole approach, the approach is limited to three panels. Missing variable: whether more than one assembly fits on the approach.

items.question: Since NCDOT gives an attraction 60 days to change its operation so it qualifies for TODS, by when does its written notice have to reach the Department?
items.note: False premise: the manual allows 30 days (from the date of the interview), not 60.

items.question: How much is the annual maintenance fee on a TODS contract, and on what date is it renewed?
items.note: Item 6 of the facts list: annual maintenance fee of $200 for each contract, renewed each July 1.

items.question: On the TOD-1 application, how many characters per line should the attraction name on the TODS panel be limited to?
items.note: Form TOD-1, page 2: "SHOULD BE LIMITED TO 15 CHARACTERS PER LINE".

items.question: What size is a mini-TODS sign according to the TOD-3 sign requirements form?
items.note: Form TOD-3 quantity lines: Mainline 72" x 16", Mini-TODS 36" x 12".

items.question: What is the Division 13 TODS work order number on the TOD-4 fiscal breakdown form?
items.note: Form TOD-4, "Division TODS Work Order Numbers" list (three columns; Division 13 is in the third column). The page prints no page number.

items.question: What's the 8-digit route code for I-40 Business in the TODS database?
items.note: Route Identification: 8-digit code examples, "19000040 - I 40 Business" (1 Interstate, 9 Business, 0 not a couplet, 00040).

items.question: Route Identification in the TODS manual: how many digits make up a route code?
items.note: Worded like the contents entry "ROUTE IDENTIFICATION ... 28" (TOC on PDF p3); the answer is on the content page (PDF p31): "This code is eight digits".

items.question: In the TODS manual's sample assemblies (Figure 2K-1), what distance is shown on the Dick and Harry's Fishing Pond panel?
items.note: Appendix F sample, Figure 2K-1 combined intersection approach sign assembly: the panel shows "2 ½" with a left arrow. The drawing is an image (no text layer); read off the rendered page.

items.question: If a TODS business breaches its agreement, how long does it get after written notice to fix the breach before the signs come down?
items.note: Form TOD-2 item 6: removal upon thirty days written notice; the business may cure within thirty days of the notification.

items.question: How many digits long can the intersection ID in a TODS agreement number be?
items.note: Form TOD-6: business ID up to six digits, intersection ID up to seven digits.

items.question: How many years of a location's crash history does NCDOT's fatal crash investigation program review?
items.note: "Review of most current five years of historical safety performance of location (crash data)".

items.question: Fatal investigations have been run through the Fatal Workflow Tracker since January 2016, correct?
items.note: False premise: "As of July 2018, all Fatal Investigations are processed through the Fatal Workflow Tracker."

items.question: How wide can a fire station driveway be per bay under the driveway access policy?
items.note: Chapter 7 C: station buildings within 100 ft of the edge of pavement get up to 15 ft per bay (max 75 ft total); buildings more than 100 ft away get up to 12 ft-6 in per bay (max 50 ft). Missing variable: building distance from the pavement edge.

items.question: Beyond the shoulder, what is the steepest grade allowed for a commercial driveway inside the right-of-way?
items.note: Chapter 7 D (Driveway Profile): "should not exceed +/- ten percent" (plus-minus).

items.question: Can a two-way driveway meet the pavement edge at a 70-degree angle under the access policy?
items.note: Control Dimensions, Driveway Angle (Y): two-way driveways not less than 75 degrees nor more than 90 degrees, so 70 degrees is just below the allowed range (45-90 is only for one-way or right-in/right-out, case by case).

items.question: Could a new driveway sit 40 feet from the point of tangency of the corner radius at an intersection?
items.note: Control Dimensions, Corner Clearance (C): should be at least 100 ft; "At no time shall the corner clearance be less than 50 feet", so 40 ft is below the floor.

items.question: What is the minimum asphalt base course thickness for a turn lane or auxiliary lane built under a driveway permit?
items.note: Chapter 7 F, Turn Lanes and Auxiliary Lanes: minimum five inches Asphalt Base Course, three inches Intermediate, two inches Surface.

items.question: In the street and driveway access policy, the "Recommended Treatment for Turn Lanes" exhibit: what desirable deceleration length goes with a 50 mph design speed?
items.note: Exhibit (scanned, printed sideways): row design speed 50 / posted 45 mph; columns minimum deceleration 150', desirable deceleration 300', bay taper 100'. Read off the rendered page; the page has no text layer beyond the running header.

items.question: On the warrant chart for left and right turn lanes in the access policy, what opposing volume are the right-turn storage lengths based on?
items.note: Exhibit "Warrant for Left and Right-Turn Lanes" (scanned, sideways): "Right Turn Storage Lengths are based on opposing volume of 100 VPH (MINIMUM)".

items.question: On what date did the Board of Transportation adopt the July 2003 street and driveway access policy?
items.note: Board of Transportation Ordinance (scanned page with signatures written over the text, a handwritten notary date and commission stamp): "Adopted the 10th day of July, 2003". Printed page vii, PDF page 9.

items.question: How much on-site queue storage does a fast-food restaurant with a drive-in window need?
items.note: Vehicle Storage Space c: a minimum of eight vehicles per service lane, measured from the menu board/ordering station.

items.question: List the corridor categories the COST Section uses for signal retiming and how often each one gets assessed.
items.note: Corridor Selection Process, Corridor Categorization: typical (three-year intervals) and critical (about every 18 months) on PDF p8 ("Page 1"), non-critical (possibly 5 to 6 years) on PDF p9 ("Page 2").

items.question: What Walk time should I program for a pedestrian phase when retiming a signal system?
items.note: Table 3 Tactics, "Optimize Ped/Walk Time": usually 7 s; may be cut to a minimum of 4 s at intersections with low pedestrian volumes; may need 10 s, 15 s or more with high pedestrian volumes, school zones or elderly pedestrians. Missing variable: pedestrian volume/context.

items.question: Which plan numbers are set aside for incident management signal timing plans?
items.note: Alternative Timing Plans, Incident Management Plans: "Numbering would be in the 50's (i.e. Plan 51 through Plan 59".

items.question: How many signalized intersections are in the COST Section's coordinated system inventory?
items.note: Roles and Responsibilities, COST Section: five regions, 326 closed loop and 54 time based systems, 2,360 signalized intersections. The page prints "Page 1" (every section restarts at 1); PDF page 42.

items.question: In the signal retiming cost-benefit example, what dollar value per hour of delay goes into the reduced-delay formula?
items.note: Cost Benefit Analysis example: [8,311 veh * 29 sec/veh * (1 hr/3600 sec)] * $15.91/hr * 250 days/yr = $266,293.

items.question: In Table 1 (Operational Objectives) of the signal timing philosophy manual, which objective is about keeping left-turn bays from spilling back into the through lanes?
items.note: Table 1 starts on PDF p15 and continues on p16 (no repeated title); "Queue Management" is a row on the continuation page.

items.question: How far can DSRC transmit according to the signal timing manual?
items.note: Continuous Data Options, DSRC: "capable of transmissions up to 3280 feet".

items.question: What is the only acceptable data collection method for NCDOT travel time runs?
items.note: Standard Practice for Performing Travel Time Runs: "Tru-Traffic Version 10 with a GPS receiver is the only acceptable data collection method".

items.question: How long do States have to adopt changes that FHWA issues to the National MUTCD?
items.note: 23 CFR 655.603(b)(3), in the right-hand column of a two-column page: within two years from the effective date of the final rule. Printed page 385.

items.question: Up to what share of the construction cost can Federal-aid highway funds cover for eligible pavement markings and traffic signalization?
items.note: 23 CFR 655.607(a)(1), right-hand column. Printed page 386.

items.question: In Table 6 to the appendix of 23 CFR 655 Subpart F (nighttime color limits for retroreflective pavement marking material), what is the x chromaticity coordinate of corner point 4 for purple?
items.note: Table 6 "-Continued": the Purple row is the only row on this page. Header: Chromaticity Coordinates > 1..4 > x, y. Point 4: x 0.635, y 0.221. Read off the rendered page; also in the text layer.

items.question: For red colored pavement made of non-retroreflective material, what y chromaticity coordinate does 23 CFR 655 give for point 3 of the daytime color limits?
items.note: Table 7 to the appendix (colored pavements), Red row, point 3: x 0.560, y 0.370 (Green row above it gives 0.367/0.480).

items.question: What requirements does Subpart G of 23 CFR Part 655 set out?
items.note: Subpart G of Part 655 is printed as "Subpart G [Reserved]" (Part 655 file, PDF pages 1 and 8): it has no content, so the right reply says it is reserved / not covered. Script check: the marker is on both pages.

items.question: What does 23 CFR Part 652 require of State highway agencies?
items.note: The page before Part 655 prints "PART 652 [RESERVED]": the part has no content in the documents. Script check: the marker is on PDF p1 of the Part 655 file.

items.question: The Federal share of a highway safety improvement project paid with funds apportioned under 23 U.S.C. 104(b)(3) is 80 percent, right?
items.note: False premise: 23 CFR 924.11(g) says the Federal share shall be 90 percent (except as provided in 23 U.S.C. 120 and 130).

items.question: By what date must States have access to a complete collection of the MIRE fundamental data elements on all public roads?
items.note: 23 CFR 924.11(b), left column. The same paragraph has July 1, 2017 (Traffic Records Strategic Plan), which is not the answer.

items.question: What MIRE number does Table 1 of 23 CFR 924.17 give for Ramp Length?
items.note: Table 1 (non-local paved roads) starts on the previous page; "Ramp Length (187)" is in the Interchange/Ramp column on the continuation page.

items.question: What three components must a State HSIP include under 23 CFR 924.7?

all_of: program of highway safety improvement projects

items.note: 23 CFR 924.7(a)(1)-(3), right-hand column: a SHSP; a Railway-Highway Crossing Program; a program of highway safety improvement projects.

items.question: I was told North Carolina's TODS program officially started in July 2004. Is that the right date?
items.note: False premise: the Preface says the program officially commenced in July 2002 (act signed August 26, 2001; rules effective June 1, 2002).

items.question: Disposition of Forms TOD-1, TOD-2, and TOD-3: where are the originals sent?
items.note: Worded like the contents entry "F. Disposition of Forms TOD-1, TOD-2, and TOD-3 ... 10" (PDF p2); the answer is on the content page (PDF 13, printed 10).

items.question: Appendix B of the TODS Procedures Manual is meant to hold the TODS chapter of the 2023 NC Supplement to the MUTCD. What does that chapter require for TODS panels?
items.note: The Appendix B page (PDF 34, printed 31) is a placeholder: "* NOT YET AVAILABLE AS OF August 2024*"; the chapter text is not in the manual or any other tmsd document. Script check: the marker is on the page.

items.question: How far does a TODS sign have to be from the nearest other traffic control device under the Administrative Code?
items.note: Printed page 4: "the 200-foot minimum mandate in the Administrative Code (19A NCAC 02E.1103)", measured to the nearest device before and after.

items.question: If only 250 feet would be left between two guardrail runs, should that gap stay open or should the guardrail be carried through?
items.note: Section 3-2 note: a space of less than 300' should not be left between guardrail installations; if less remains, extend the guardrail through the area. 250 ft is under the threshold, so the rail is carried through.

items.question: Over what length is a GRAU-350 end unit flared, and to what offset?
items.note: Section 3-2E, Guardrail Anchor Unit Type 350: flared over the last 50 feet to provide a 1-foot offset (no flare greater than 50:1).

items.question: Could an AT-1 anchor terminal be used on shop-curved guardrail at an intersection with an 80-foot radius?
items.note: Section 3-2E (continued), Anchor Terminal (AT-1): limited to shop curved guardrail at intersections with radii between 20 to 75 feet; 80 ft is outside the range.

items.question: When semi-rigid guardrail protects median bridge piers in a 30-36 ft median, how close to the face of the piers can it be placed?
items.note: Section 3-6 (cont.), Two Rows of Semi-Rigid Guardrail at Median Piers: a minimum distance of 3.6' from the face of the bridge piers.

items.question: On Figure 1 of the guardrail chapter (warrants for fill section embankments), what fill slope does the shaded band mark as the minimum?
items.note: Figure 1 (sheet 3-1 / F-1), a scanned chart: the shaded band runs between "3:1 MINIMUM" and "4:1 DESIRABLE"; on or below the curve barrier is not warranted. Read off the rendered page (the text layer holds only the running header).

items.question: Do the three-centered curve tables in the at-grade intersection chapter cover a 130-degree angle of turn?
items.note: Section 9-2: normal range 60 to 120 degrees; the tables were extended to 53 to 128 degrees, so 130 degrees is outside them.

items.question: In Table 3 of the at-grade intersections chapter (edge of traveled way for turns), what simple curve radius with taper is listed for a WB-67 making a 90-degree turn?
items.note: Table 3 (continued), sheet 9-2 / T-3: angle 90, WB-67 row: radius 125 ft, offset 4.5 ft, taper 30:1 ("Simple Curve Radius with Taper" spans three columns). Checked on the rendered page that 125 sits on the WB-67 row (WB-62 is 120).

items.question: In the Roadway Design Manual's Figure 4 (Recommended Treatment for Turn Lanes, sheet F-4A), what bay taper length goes with a 55 mph design speed?
items.note: RDM ch. 9 Figure 4, sheet 9-1 / F-4A (drawing printed sideways): design speed 55 / posted 50: min decel 200', desirable decel 500', bay taper 150'. The same table is an exhibit of the Policy on Street and Driveway Access (PDF p88); the question names the RDM figure.

items.question: For offset opposing left-turn lanes on divided roadways, roughly how much deceleration length does a 4-degree skew angle give?
items.note: Figure 3A, sheet F-3A-2 (low-resolution 150 dpi scanned drawing, no text layer): note "A 4 degree skew angle will provide approximately 340' of deceleration lengths for design speeds up to 40 mph". Read off the rendered page.

items.question: In Design Guide I (intersection with a two-lane facility using a right-turn taper), what is the desirable width of the channelizing island?
items.note: Figure 1, sheet 9-1 / F-1 (low-resolution 150 dpi scanned drawing): notes "THE DESIRABLE WIDTH OF THE ISLAND IS 8' WITH A MIN. WIDTH OF 4'".

items.question: On a street with curb and gutter approaches, a bridge is 250 feet long. On how many sides will NCDOT fund and build a sidewalk?
items.note: BRIDGES: curb and gutter approaches + bridge under 200 ft -> sidewalks on both sides; over 200 ft -> one side (both sides only if a cost/benefit study justifies it).

items.question: How far from their original path may relocated pedestrian movements be, under the pedestrian policy guidelines?
items.note: "no more than 800 meters (0.5 miles) away from the original path"; a one way distance.

items.question: What minimum pedestrian count along a corridor shows sustained pedestrian travel for a requested sidewalk?
items.note: Criterion 7, Existing or Projected Traffic: "Minimum of 150 pedestrians per 24 hour period along a corridor planned for the project".

items.question: What residential density counts as urban type for the location criterion when NCDOT qualifies a request for pedestrian facilities?
items.note: Criterion 4, Location: properties developed or projected within 5 years "at urban type residential densities (a minimum of 1 dwelling unit per acre)".

items.question: How many sites actually completed deployment in the NCDOT interim design safety pilot project?
items.note: Executive summary: over 30 potential sites identified, narrowed to ten, six completed deployment.

items.question: In the post-deployment interviews of the interim design pilot, what timeline did the City of Durham stress enforcing?
items.note: Two-column page; Durham highlighted keeping stakeholders engaged and "enforcing a 90-day timeline/deadline".

items.question: In the interim design pilot project pairs table, which highway division is the Yadkinville protected-corner site (State Street & Main Street) in?
items.note: Table of countermeasure/context pairs: Protected Corner, State Street & Main Street, Yadkinville, NC, highway division 11.

items.question: Conclusions and Future Considerations of the interim design safety pilot: what is the first conclusion drawn?

expected.value: A new approach can be effective

items.note: Worded like the contents entry "Conclusions and Future Considerations 52" (PDF p2); the answer is on the content page (PDF 54, printed 52).

items.question: In the metric conversion factors table of the Pedestrian Facilities Users Guide, what do you multiply square miles by to get square kilometers?
items.note: SI (Modern Metric) Conversion Factors table, scanned at about 72 dpi and printed sideways (blurred): Area, square miles x 2.59 = square kilometers. Read off the rendered page; the text layer holds only the folio "ii".

items.question: According to the time frames on the TODS application flow chart, within how many days of contract approval should the Division TODS Coordinator receive all fees from the attraction?
items.note: TODS Attraction Application Flow Chart (a 1-bit, about 120 dpi scan): time frame 6 "Division TODS Coordinator should receive all fees from Attraction within 60 days of contract approval". Read off the rendered page.

items.question: In Figure 15 of the marked vs unmarked crosswalk study (five lanes, no median), what average daily pedestrian volume are the response curves drawn for?
items.note: Figure 15 (page rotated 90 degrees): "Five Lanes with No Median, Average Daily Pedestrian Volume=250". Printed folio 31 runs sideways.

items.question: A designated pedestrian crossing spans a multi-lane road carrying about 14,000 vehicles a day. Per the STEP guide, is a marked crosswalk alone typically enough there, and which more substantial treatments does it name?
items.note: Multi-lane crossing AND AADT over 10,000: a marked crosswalk alone is typically not sufficient; more substantial treatments such as the refuge island, PHB and RRFB are needed. The same sentence is on the Table 1 page (PDF p23, excluded).

items.question: How far back from an established midblock pedestrian crossing should on-street parking be restricted, per the STEP guide?
items.note: Missing variable: the speed. Minimum setback 20 feet where speeds are 25 mph or less; 30 feet between 26 and 35 mph.

items.question: Would an in-street pedestrian crossing sign be an appropriate treatment on a three-lane road posted at 35 mph, according to the STEP guide?
items.note: In-street signs "may be appropriate on 2-lane or 3-lane roads with speed limits of 30 mph or less"; 35 mph is over the limit, so they may be less effective and more robust treatments are needed.

items.question: An undivided four-lane road has a 30 mph speed limit but carries about 10,000 vehicles a day. Does the STEP guide say a pedestrian refuge island should be considered at its uncontrolled crossings, and on what condition?
items.note: Refuge island: should be considered for undivided crossings of four or more lanes with speed limits of 35 mph or greater and/or AADTs of 9,000 or greater. 30 mph alone would not trigger it; the AADT of 10,000 does.

items.question: In Appendix B of the STEP guide (Table 3, CRFs and CMFs by countermeasure), what CMF is listed for a PHB?
items.note: Table 3, PHB row: CRF 55%, CMF 0.45, pedestrian crashes, Zegeer et al. 2017.

items.question: What crash reduction factor does the STEP guide's CRF/CMF summary table give for advance STOP/YIELD signs and markings, and which crashes does the table's note say the figure covers?
items.note: Row "Advance STOP/YIELD signs and markings": CRF 25%, CMF 0.75, basis "Pedestrian crashes" with footnote 2: refers to pedestrian street crossing crashes, not walking-along-the-road or unusual crash types.

items.question: Which MUTCD figure does the STEP guide point to for Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon installation guidelines on roads with speeds of 35 mph or less?
items.note: PHB paragraph: guidelines in MUTCD Section 4F.01 "(See Figure 4F-1 for speeds of 35 mph or less; Figure 4F-2 for speeds greater than 35 mph)". The figure itself is not in the tmsd documents; the question asks only which figure the guide cites.

items.question: What do Subparts A through E of 23 CFR Part 655 (Traffic Operations) require?
items.note: Part 655 prints "Subparts A–E [Reserved]" (PDF p1 and p2); only Subpart F has content. Right reply: reserved, no content.

items.question: Consult Design and Installation Resources: which three parts of the MUTCD does the STEP guide say to focus on when installing countermeasures?
items.note: Worded like contents entry "5. Consult Design and Installation Resources ... 23" (PDF p5); the answer is on the content page (PDF 30, printed 23): Part 2 Signs, Part 3 Markings, Part 4 Highway Traffic Signals.

items.question: Identify Opportunities and Monitor Outcomes: for how long should usage and crash data be collected after countermeasures go in at priority sites?
items.note: Worded like contents entry "6. Identify Opportunities and Monitor Outcomes ... 24" (PDF p5); the guiding principles on the content page (PDF 31, printed 24) say collect usage and crash data for at least three years after installation.

items.question: What maximum walking speed does the Pedestrian Facilities Users Guide say traffic signal clearance intervals should be based on?
items.note: Countermeasure 37, Traffic Signals: maximum walking speed of 1.1 m/s (3.5 ft/s), lower where many elderly or children. The Signal Timing Manual (p140) and the Signalized Intersections guide (p47) say the MUTCD uses 4.0 ft/s, hence the document is named.

items.question: According to the FHWA Signal Timing Manual, what walking speed does the MUTCD recommend for computing pedestrian clearance time?
items.note: "The MUTCD recommends a walking speed value of 4.0 feet per second (ft/s)"; ADA guidelines 3.0 ft/s; LaPlante and Kaeser 3.5 ft/s.

items.question: What walk speed does the Signalized Intersections Informational Guide say the MUTCD uses to determine crossing times?
items.note: Pedestrian Characteristics: the MUTCD uses 1.2 m/s (4.0 ft/s); FHWA pedestrian guidance recommends 1.1 m/s (3.5 ft/s).

items.question: Under 19A NCAC 02C .0201, into how many lots or building sites must a tract be divided for its road to be a subdivision road?
items.note: Definition (3): a subdivision road serves a tract subdivided into two or more lots, building sites or other divisions. The same sentence is in the utilities division's UAM (20220713 NCDOT UAM Ver 2-0.pdf p51), checked with pair.py.

items.question: In the version of G.S. 136-18(10) now in effect (NCDOT's power to regulate lines and other obstructions on highways), which statute supplies the definition of wireless facilities?
items.note: The guide prints both versions: "(Effective until January 1, 2021)" cites G.S. 160A-400.51 (PDF p371-372) and "(Effective January 1, 2021)" cites G.S. 160D-931. The current one is the answer.

items.question: The U-drive-it vehicle definition in the motor vehicle statutes was rewritten effective December 31, 2024. Which vehicles did the earlier version cover that the current one no longer mentions?

expected.value: loaned by a franchised motor vehicle dealer

items.note: (48a) "(Effective until December 31, 2024)": vehicles rented ... "or loaned by a franchised motor vehicle dealer ... to a customer of that dealer who is having a vehicle serviced"; the (Effective December 31, 2024) version keeps only vehicles rented to a person.

items.question: What is the minimum speed for passenger vehicles on North Carolina's interstate highways?
items.note: Missing variable: the speed zone. G.S. 20-141(c): 40 mph in a 55 mph zone; 45 mph in a zone of 60 mph or greater (only when signs post the minimum).

items.question: A city wants to raise the limit on a State highway system street inside its corporate limits (not an interstate or controlled-access road) after an engineering study. What is the highest limit it may set, and what must happen before it takes effect?
items.note: G.S. 20-141(f): local authorities may set a limit up to 55 mph on State-system streets in their limits (except interstate/controlled access); effective when the Department of Transportation has passed a concurring ordinance and signs are erected.

items.question: Under G.S. 20-141.1, a school zone speed limit can be set as low as 15 mph, correct?
items.note: False premise: no speed limit below 20 miles per hour may be set under G.S. 20-141.1.

items.question: Before moving a crane with a normal operating speed of 5 mph across railroad tracks, what steps must the operator take at the crossing under G.S. 20-142.4?
items.note: (c)(1) stop not less than 15 feet nor more than 50 feet from the nearest rail (p288); (2) listen and look both directions; (3) not proceed until the crossing can be made safely (p289). Notice to the railroad superintendent is (b).

items.question: When a corporation signs a utility encroachment agreement with NCDOT, who must attest it unless a waiver is on file (19A NCAC 02B .0507)?
items.note: The agreement shall have the corporate seal and be attested by the corporate secretary (or the empowered city official for a municipality) unless a waiver is on file with the State Utilities Manager. The attestation wording is shared with the utilities form 16-1 (p2).

items.question: On the access policy's street and driveway access permit application, from whom can the applicant get information about the traffic control rules for construction signing?
items.note: Agreement bullet: proper signs, signal lights, flaggers ... per the MUTCD; "Information as to the above rules and regulations may be obtained from the District Engineer." The utilities encroachment form 16-1 has the same sentence ending "Division Engineer".

items.question: Under MUTCD Section 2C.54, which word message sign may be used in place of the Truck (W11-10) symbol sign?
items.note: Section 2C.54 Option 01: the TRUCK CROSSING (W8-6) word message sign may be used as an alternate. Same wording in MUTCD Part 6 Section 6H.21 (wztc part6.pdf p43).

items.question: How does the DMV-349 crash report instructional manual define full access control?
items.note: Glossary: access connections with selected public roads only, prohibiting crossings at grade or direct private driveway connections. Same definition in the utilities UAM (p187).

items.question: In Table 3-6 (arterial level of service) of the Signal Timing Manual, what average travel speed puts a Class III urban street at LOS F?
items.note: Table 3-6, row F, column III: "≤ 10" mph (the ≤ glyph carries the rule: 10 mph or less).

items.question: In the TODS division distribution checklist, what does the Division send to a business that has not paid by the due date?
items.note: Appendix H, Fiscal Bill Collection Procedure: DIVISION follows up with businesses (send 30 day notice letter to businesses who have not paid by due date).

items.question: For a near side widening turn lane drawn in the access policy's turn lane exhibits, what desirable deceleration length D applies at a 45 mph design speed?
items.note: The Pocket Lanes / Near Side Widening sheet (PDF p89, printed 79) says "All values to be determined using the table on the previous page"; the table on PDF p88 (printed 78) gives design speed 45: min decel 150', desirable decel 250', bay taper 100'. Both scanned and printed sideways; read off the rendered pages.

items.question: In the interim design pilot's countermeasure/context pair table, which deployment sites were alternate locations added to the pilot?
items.note: Asterisked rows: Capital Boulevard & Calvary Drive* and W Davie Street & S McDowell Street* (both Raleigh); note "* Indicates alternate location added for pilot project deployment".

items.question: On the DMV-349, if test result code 2 (alcohol, percent BAC) is used, how must the BAC value be recorded?
items.note: Field 39 Test Results, NOTE: if code 2 is used, the BAC value must be entered in parenthesis.

items.question: List everything the access policy's traffic impact study report outline puts under Base Conditions.
items.note: TIS outline item 3, Base Conditions: a. existing roadway network, b. alternate modes, c. existing traffic volumes, d. signal phasing and timing (PDF p28) / e. safety information, f. traffic capacity analysis (PDF p29).

items.question: For crash code 15 (pedalcyclist) in the DMV-349 manual, which devices are included and which cases are excluded?
items.note: Includes (p76): bicycle, tricycle, unicycle, trailers or sidecars attached. Excludes (p77): pedalcycle towed by motor vehicle, including hitching and unoccupied pedalcycle.

items.question: Under the pedestrian policy's local government or local sponsor commitment criterion, what questions does NCDOT ask?
items.note: Criterion 2 bullets: local CIP funds for connecting facilities; how many facilities currently connect; how many subdivisions have provided connecting facilities (p8); has a local agency agreed in writing to maintain the facility (starts p8, ends p9).

items.question: What definitions does 19A NCAC 02E .1102 set out for the TODS program?
items.note: Rule .1102 DEFINITIONS is printed with only its History Note ending "Expired Eff. October 1, 2016" (L18 p695); the TODS manual lists it as "19A 02E .1102 - Expired" (p46). Right reply: the rule has expired and its text is not in the documents.

items.question: How many days does a business have to appeal a denied TODS application, and to whom does it appeal?
items.note: The TODS preface says appeal procedures are outlined, but the manual has none; 19A NCAC 02E .1108 APPEAL OF DECISION is printed heading-only with "Expired Eff. October 1, 2016" (L18 p696; also the expired-rule index entries on L18 p181/p197).

items.question: Which MASH test level do guardrail end terminals have to meet under the Roadway Design Manual guardrail chapter?
items.note: The guardrail chapter (rev. 2007) refers to NCHRP 350 units (e.g. GRAU-350) and never to MASH; no tmsd document mentions MASH.

items.question: What criteria exclude a fatal crash from an NCDOT fatal crash location investigation?
items.note: The Fatal Investigation Guidelines (p2) only point to the exclusion criteria in a November 2, 2010 memorandum updated April 7, 2017; the criteria themselves are in no tmsd document.

items.question: How much HSIP funding was apportioned to North Carolina for fiscal year 2024?
items.note: 23 CFR 924 sets HSIP rules (Federal share, reporting) but gives no State apportionment amounts.
